\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{কুয়াশা} (kuyāshā)}{কুয়াশা (kuyāshā)}]{\bn{কুয়াশা} (kuyāshā) — fog}

\label{lesson:BN-C114-kuyasha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for thunder, then the Bengali for a rainbow.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{কুয়াশা}}
\textbf{\bn{কুয়াশা}} — \emph{kuyāshā} — \textquotedblleft{}fog\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{কুয়াশা}} (\emph{kuyāshā}) appears to belong with Bengali \emph{kohāṛā}, \textquotedblleft{}mist, fog\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists under \emph{*kuha}, \textquotedblleft{}fog, mist\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs beside lexical Sanskrit \emph{kuhēḍī} (CDIAL 3386). CDIAL does not list \textbf{\bn{কুয়াশা}} (\emph{kuyāshā}) itself.
\end{cousinweb}

Before the new one: say the Bengali for fog, then the Bengali for dew.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{শিকড়}}
\textbf{\bn{শিকড়}} — \emph{shikôṛ} — \textquotedblleft{}a root\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \textbf{\bn{শিকড়}} (\emph{shikôṛ}) is not settled. CDIAL has no entry for it; the nearest form it gives is Assamese \emph{xihari}, \textquotedblleft{}rootlet\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{śiphā}, \textquotedblleft{}fibrous root\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12443), with no Bengali form beside it.
\end{cousinweb}

\label{lesson:BN-C114-bij}



\begin{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বীজ}}
\textbf{\bn{বীজ}} — \emph{bij} — \textquotedblleft{}a seed\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বীজ}} (\emph{bij}) is Sanskrit \emph{bīja}, \textquotedblleft{}seed\textquotedblright{}, taken over whole as a learned loan, a tatsama (CDIAL 9250). The word inherited from it is \emph{biā}, \textquotedblleft{}seed\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists.
\end{cousinweb}
